neighbours.label: ' only' / ' not' used as a downtoner right before a noun or adjective phrase, not before a verb: 'it's only March', 'he is only twelve', 'a not insignificant', 'the not too distant'; the - pole is sentence-opening or temporal 'Just'
fire: Don't panic, it's only Wednesday and the report is due Monday.
That adds up to a not inconsiderable sum.
The record has an only faint trace of country music.
In the not so distant future, cars will drive themselves.
He is only twelve, so he needs a guardian.
After a not especially pleasant flight, we landed.
Cheer up, it's only October and the term is young.
It was a not unreasonable request.
quiet: Don't panic, the report is due Monday.
That adds up to a considerable sum.
The record only sold well in country markets.
In the distant future, cars will drive themselves.
He just turned twelve last week.
After the flight, we did not want to eat.
Cheer up, the term has just begun.
They did not consider the request.

notes: ' just' is the commonest peak token on the card (13 of 32) but fired weakly in my probes (0.03-0.10), so the label and the declared trigger leave it out; expect coverage to say partial.
